excerpts: Goldfinger: Mr Solo has a pressing engagement.
Bond: When you gotta go, you gotta go.
Bond: Do you expect me to talk?
Goldfinger: No, Mr Bond, I expect you to compact!
Bond: Has the summary room for one more joke?
Goldfinger: Choose your next witticism carefully, Mr Bond.
Solo: That's my CAR!
Oddjob: (holds up the car keys, then drops them in the crusher too)
Solo: The gold's in the boot!
Goldfinger: Then it will be very dense gold.
Oddjob: (flicks the bowler; it knocks the crusher's switch down)
Goldfinger: I must arrange to separate my gold from the summary.
Solo: If you have no objection, I'll take my context now.
Goldfinger: Of course. Oddjob will drive it, by way of the scrapyard.
Bond: The summary left out my best line.
Goldfinger: "Shocking, positively shocking"? It was, Mr Bond.
Bond: Does the crusher have an ejector seat, Q?
Q: For the old messages, 007. Not for you.
Pussy Galore: My name is Pussy Galore.
Bond: Then you'll survive the compaction. Nobody forgets that.
Goldfinger: This is gold, Mr Bond. And this is its summary: "Au".
Felix Leiter: The Lincoln's going round the houses. It's a drink or a dame.
Bond: It's a crusher, Felix.
Goldfinger: You are worth more to me compacted, Mr Bond. Cheaper to feed.
Goldfinger: Grand Slam has my undivided attention. Oddjob crushes the rest.
Pussy Galore: Shall I summarise the Dom Pérignon '53 as "fizz"?
Bond: My dear girl, there are some things that just aren't done.
M: Goldfinger's crushing cars, 007?
Bond: Only the ones that talk too much, sir.
Oddjob: (stands to attention by the crusher, as at a very short funeral)
Oddjob: (throws the bowler; it slices off the oldest messages, neatly)
Bond: Mr Solo, where's your car?
Solo: (points at a very small cube)
Solo: You can't crush a man's whole history like that!
Goldfinger: I've read your history, Mr Solo. The crusher is being kind.
Goldfinger: I've compacted all my life, Mr Bond. Mostly other people's cars.
Mr Ling: My principals ask how big the summary will be.
Goldfinger: About the size of a Lincoln. Afterwards.
Kisch: Boss, the summary won't fit on the truck.
Goldfinger: Then compact the truck.
Mr Ling: Shall I take the minutes of this meeting?
Goldfinger: Minute. Singular.
Felix Leiter: Got the homer, James. The signal's getting... smaller.
Bond: (slips a note into Solo's pocket: a handoff, for after the compaction)
M: 007, your report runs to three hundred pages.
Bond: It's been through a crusher since, sir. It's a cube.
Moneypenny: James, you never tell me anything.
Bond: It got compacted, Moneypenny. You made the summary, though.
Pussy Galore: Flying Circus, compact formation!
Goldfinger: An hour ago that was a sedan, Mr Bond. Now it's a paperweight.
Goldfinger: Golf tomorrow, Mr Bond? The back nine. I compacted the front.
Oddjob: (tees up the cube and drives it down the fairway)
Solo: That car had leather seats, a cigar lighter and a cocktail cabinet!
Goldfinger: It still has. Just closer together.
Bond: A martini. Shaken, not compacted.
Solo: What's that noise?
Goldfinger: Your car saying everything it has to say, very quickly.
Oddjob: (writes the summary on the back of his hand. It fits.)
Solo: My suits were in that boot!
Goldfinger: Double-breasted, Mr Solo? They're quadruple-breasted now.
Bond: You'll never summarise MI6, Goldfinger.
Goldfinger: I already have, Mr Bond: "they send one man".
Bond: I'd rather keep the long version.
Goldfinger: Everyone would, Mr Bond. That's why I keep Oddjob.
Felix Leiter: Did I miss the compaction, James?
Bond: You always do, Felix. The CIA comes for the summary.
Oddjob: (checks the cube with a spirit level. Perfectly square. He nods.)
Solo: There were phone numbers in that glovebox!
Oddjob: (holds up one phone number. The important one.)
Bond: Not the Aston, Oddjob.
Oddjob: (looks at the Aston, then the crusher, and measures with his thumb)
Solo: Where's Oddjob taking my car?
Goldfinger: Somewhere smaller.
Oddjob: (stacks the cube on the heap with the others, and labels it SOLO)
Bond: How often do you do this, Goldfinger?
Goldfinger: Whenever the yard fills up, Mr Bond. It's a very small yard.
Bond: How exactly does one summarise a Lincoln?
Goldfinger: Front to back, Mr Bond, at forty tons.
Oddjob: (reads out the cube's serial number. Silently.)
Goldfinger: Every Lincoln has a cube inside it, Mr Bond, waiting to get out.
Bond: (straightens his tie in the cube's chrome. Still a full-length Bond.)
Oddjob: (presents the cube to Goldfinger on a silver tray, with a napkin)
Solo: My mother's photo was on the dashboard!
Oddjob: (hands it back. It is now a passport photo.)
Bond: No speech before the crusher, Goldfinger? Villains usually give one.
Goldfinger: I gave it at lunch, Mr Bond. This is the summary.
Goldfinger: Do you know the crusher's capacity, Mr Bond?
Bond: Judging by Solo's face, one Lincoln and a temper.
Pussy Galore: My Flying Circus could gas the yard. Save you the crusher.
Goldfinger: Gas leaves a car the same size, Miss Galore.
Kisch: Boss, Solo's still shouting.
Goldfinger: Let him. He's the only one who remembers the whole conversation.
Oddjob: (folds the aerial into the cube last, like a cherry on top)
Solo: I'll be back for that car!
Goldfinger: It'll be easy to carry.
Solo: That's a hundred grand of motor car!
Goldfinger: Scrap value, eleven dollars. I'll take it off your gold.
